dismissed.why: The gap rests on the evidence’s 0.1.78 check (1 October, mirror v0.1.78 at 5b6894b) and on a re-check of the installed build, as the flow asks: a gap names the installed build it still holds on and the Component Bug proposed for it (Checkbox’s gap names #535 the same way). On 29 October, on 0.1.78-dbe0e02, FavoriteToggle.tsx still sets a hit slop of (44 − size) / 2 on each side (lines 86–89, 197 and 245), react-native-web 0.21.2’s View forwards no hitSlop prop (exports/View/index.js 26–33 picks only listed props; only the legacy Touchable mixin reads it), and in headless Chrome on the guide’s In context toggle (29 × 29) a click 5 px outside its right edge left aria-checked false, while a click inside set it true. That phones honour the hit slop is the guide’s own copy, not the evidence’s: Sizing says “On phones its tap area reaches 44 px around the circle” and the Sources note “On iOS and Android a hit slop extends the tap area to 44 px” (the Sizing sentence is quoted in this entry’s /accessibility/3); React Native’s Pressable takes hitSlop on iOS and Android. The gap names Component Bug #541, filed for it in this run.
